correctness.rationale: I rederived the minimax on the closed first-quadrant edge x=(u(1−t),vt). Squared distance has its boundary maximum at a vertex; quadrant signs make the two negative-axis vertices dominate. Their squared distances divided by v² are r(2−t)²+t² and r(1−t)²+(1+t)². The first strictly decreases up to t=1, including the square where its derivative vanishes only at that endpoint. The crossing t*=(3r−1)/(2(r+1)) is exactly 1/2 to the right of the second quadratic's vertex. Thus the envelope has its unique edge minimum at t* for 1≤r<3, and at 1 otherwise, including equality at r=3. Substitution and the four sign symmetries give the stated values and all centers (four interior-to-edge centers collapsing onto two short-diagonal endpoints). For the area ratio the derivative on the first branch has sign (r−1)(r²−14r+1), negative on 1<r≤3, versus positive for r>3; its unique minimum is 2/√3 at r=3. The ratio δ²/(u²+v²) decreases from 5/4 to 1 and is thereafter constant, yielding both L/δ bounds and their exact equality sets. The angle relation is r=cot²(φ/2). No degenerate rhombus is included. The frozen rational checker was inspected, not executed; its grid is not needed for the continuous proof.
